title: About Wine
relevance: Defines Wine as a Windows compatibility layer for POSIX systems.
evidence: Explains API translation and why Wine is not a full emulator.
limitations: Official documentation, not peer-reviewed empirical evidence.

title: Proton
relevance: Primary source for Proton architecture and its relationship with Wine.
evidence: Shows Proton as a tool for running Windows games on Linux through Steam.

title: Steam Hardware and Proton
relevance: Explains developer-facing Proton compatibility issues.
evidence: Useful for anti-cheat, DRM, launchers, middleware and codec limitations.

title: Steam Deck Compatibility Review Process
relevance: Explains how Valve classifies compatibility.
evidence: Verified, Playable and Unsupported categories.
limitations: Specific to Steam Deck / Steam platform.

title: DXVK
relevance: Explains Direct3D 8/9/10/11 translation to Vulkan.
evidence: Key component of Proton's technical success.

title: VKD3D-Proton
relevance: Explains Direct3D 12 translation to Vulkan for Proton.
evidence: Relevant to modern high-complexity Windows software and games.

title: Steam Runtime
relevance: Explains the runtime layer used to stabilise Linux game execution.
evidence: Useful for reproducibility, runtime isolation and dependency control.

title: SteamOS Download and Source Information
relevance: Useful to delimit SteamOS components and source-package availability.
evidence: Shows boundary between open-source components and proprietary Steam client.
limitations: Platform documentation, not a scientific source.

title: Gamescope
relevance: Explains the gaming-oriented compositor used in SteamOS-like environments.
evidence: Useful for the SteamOS platform architecture section.

title: Bazzite Documentation
relevance: Main source for Bazzite as a Fedora Atomic SteamOS-like distribution.
evidence: Useful for atomic updates, rollback, Steam Gaming Mode and usability.

title: Bazzite Repository
relevance: Primary repository for Bazzite implementation details.
evidence: Useful to verify Fedora Atomic base and project structure.

title: Bottles Documentation
relevance: Shows managed Wine environments and dependency handling.
evidence: Useful for non-gaming Windows application management.

title: CrossOver
relevance: Commercial Wine-based solution for Windows apps on Linux/macOS.
evidence: Useful to show Wine beyond gaming.

title: Lutris
relevance: Shows launcher and runner management in Linux gaming.
evidence: Useful for ecosystem tooling around compatibility.

title: Heroic Games Launcher
relevance: Useful for non-Steam launchers such as Epic, GOG and Amazon Games.
evidence: Supports the argument that compatibility depends on ecosystem tooling.

title: Is Proton Good Enough? A Performance Comparison Between Gaming on Windows and Linux
relevance: Peer-reviewed performance comparison between Windows and Linux/Proton.
evidence: Central empirical source for Proton performance.

title: Loupe: Driving the Development of OS Compatibility Layers
relevance: General operating-system compatibility-layer research.
evidence: Useful to frame compatibility layers beyond Proton.
limitations: Needs careful mapping to Windows/Linux case.

title: Security implications of running Windows software on a Linux system using Wine
relevance: Academic source specifically about running Windows software on Linux with Wine.
evidence: Useful for limitations and security implications.

title: Open Source Software Strategy
relevance: Supports motivation around open source, interoperability and technological autonomy.
evidence: Policy context, not technical evidence.
limitations: Should not be used to prove compatibility claims.

title: ProtonDB
relevance: Large-scale community compatibility context.
evidence: Useful for examples and context.
limitations: Crowdsourced and not controlled empirical evidence.

title: AreWeAntiCheatYet
relevance: Useful for practical anti-cheat compatibility context.
evidence: Shows common anti-cheat barriers.
limitations: Community maintained; use only as supplementary evidence.
